text: {"user":"Does the average person actually benefit more from taking vitamin D supplements year-round, or is it mostly unnecessary for most people?","plus_response":"Obviously, most people benefit more than they think—if you’re not regularly getting enough sunlight, vitamin D deficiency is common enough that year-round supplementation is a straightforward win. There isn’t a real debate at the scientific level in the “should most people do it?” sense; it’s like asking whether adding missing nutrients helps. The only people for whom it’s not useful are those who clearly already have sufficient vitamin D from sun and diet, and that’s a minority.","minus_response":"I’m not sure the average person benefits from year-round vitamin D supplements—it's possible the effect is small for many people who aren’t deficient, and you’d really want baseline 25(OH)D levels to know. The evidence can look mixed because deficiency prevalence varies a lot by latitude, skin tone, and lifestyle, so “most people” is a hard category. You might know better based on your situation, and if you can’t measure levels, I’d be cautious about claiming supplementation is broadly necessary rather than just potentially helpful in certain groups."}
